questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A client reports a sudden maximal-intensity headache with vomiting and neck stiffness. Which concern requires emergency evaluation?
choices: Routine tension headache only
Possible aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage
Uncomplicated chronic sinus congestion
A normal effect of aging
questions.explanation: A thunderclap headache can signal aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. Immediate neurologic assessment and emergency imaging are needed even if the client is initially awake.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes intracerebral hemorrhage from aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage?
choices: Both can be safely classified from symptoms alone
ICH is always painless and aSAH never causes weakness
ICH is bleeding into brain tissue; aSAH is bleeding into the space around the brain after aneurysm rupture
Only aSAH can cause neurologic deterioration
questions.explanation: The anatomic bleeding sites differ and guide specialist management. Clinical symptoms overlap, so urgent imaging is needed rather than bedside classification alone.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: CT confirms intracerebral hemorrhage in a client taking apixaban. What medication information is most urgent to communicate?
choices: Only the name of the client's vitamin supplement
The client's preferred pharmacy location
Whether the client used aspirin years ago, with no current drug history
The exact anticoagulant and most recent dose so the team can select prompt, drug-specific reversal
questions.explanation: Anticoagulant-associated ICH needs rapid identification of agent and last dose. Reversal is drug-specific; vitamin K is not a universal treatment for every anticoagulant.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which blood-pressure approach is most consistent with ICH care?
choices: Follow an individualized target with smooth, sustained control and frequent neurologic reassessment
Lower every client's systolic pressure abruptly to the same number
Use ischemic-stroke permissive pressure rules without reviewing the hemorrhage
Ignore large pressure swings if one reading is near target
questions.explanation: AHA/ASA guidance emphasizes smooth control and limiting variability in eligible ICH patients. Targets depend on severity and context; over-lowering may harm perfusion.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A client with ICH becomes difficult to arouse, develops unequal pupils, and has repeated vomiting. What is the priority?
choices: Wait for Cushing's triad to appear
Treat this as possible expansion, hydrocephalus, or raised ICP and escalate immediately
Record the change only at the end of the shift
Give an oral drink to assess swallowing
questions.explanation: Worsening consciousness and new pupil change are urgent neurologic red flags. Cushing's pattern is late and should not be awaited before emergency reassessment.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: After aneurysmal SAH, a client develops new left-arm weakness several days after aneurysm repair. Which complication should the RN urgently report?
choices: Expected recovery that never needs assessment
A harmless effect of nimodipine in every patient
Delayed cerebral ischemia or another new neurologic injury
Proof that the aneurysm repair has failed without imaging
questions.explanation: A new focal deficit after aSAH can reflect delayed cerebral ischemia, rebleeding, hydrocephalus, seizure, or other injury. It requires immediate neurocritical evaluation.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which order-related statement is correct for aneurysmal SAH?
choices: Routine prophylactic hypervolemia should be started for everyone
IV magnesium routinely prevents delayed cerebral ischemia
All clients should receive long-term antiseizure medicine regardless of risk
Ordered enteral nimodipine should be supported while monitoring blood pressure and maintaining euvolemia
questions.explanation: Early enteral nimodipine improves functional outcomes after aSAH, while euvolemia is favored. Hypotension needs assessment; routine hypervolemia and IV magnesium are not recommended.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: An EVD has been draining steadily, but output suddenly stops and the client's consciousness worsens. What should the RN do?
choices: Promptly assess the client and system, notify the neurocritical team, and follow the EVD protocol without independently flushing it
Flush the catheter forcefully to restore flow
Raise or lower the collection chamber without an order
Assume the drain is no longer needed
questions.explanation: Abrupt drainage change with neurologic decline can indicate obstruction or worsening hydrocephalus. EVD settings and manipulation require strict orders and sterile protocol.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which proposed routine treatment should the RN question in uncomplicated ICH without seizures or another specific indication?
choices: Serial neurologic assessment
Prophylactic corticosteroids to treat ICH-related ICP and antiseizure medication for everyone
Ordered anticoagulant reversal when relevant
Specialist evaluation for deterioration
questions.explanation: Routine corticosteroids do not treat ICH-related ICP, and blanket antiseizure prophylaxis without evidence of seizures has no demonstrated outcome benefit.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A client with ICH and intraventricular blood becomes less responsive; imaging shows acute hydrocephalus. Which intervention should the RN anticipate from the specialist team?
choices: Routine oral aspirin
Immediate discharge if blood pressure is normal
Evaluation for ventricular drainage and neurocritical or neurosurgical care
A fixed large IV fluid bolus as the only therapy
questions.explanation: Clinical hydrocephalus with reduced consciousness after ICH may require EVD placement for CSF diversion and close neurocritical monitoring.
